comparator.name: Global Management of Social Issues
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-taught track has 60 EC each year. The third-year mobility window allows 30 EC of approved study or an internship, including specified combinations. Students complete a 12 EC individual thesis in the final semester.

components.name: Wicked Problems 101
components.note: GROW mentoring and personal development continue across the three years and carry no credits.

components.name: Introduction to Statistics
components.note: The ordinary first-year binding study advice threshold is 42 EC from the first-year curriculum.

components.name: History of Government and Public Institutions
Fundamentals of International Law and EU Law
Advanced Project Management
components.note: Financial and Project Management, or equivalent prior knowledge, prepares students for this course’s work on projects involving multiple organisations and stakeholders.

components.name: Wicked Problems 201: Research Practicum
components.note: Causal Analysis Techniques prepares students to analyse quantitative data and write a research paper. Working-group attendance is required.

components.name: Mobility Window: Approved Study or Internship
components.note: Choose 30 EC of approved study or an internship, or a permitted combination. Internships can carry 12, 18, 24 or 30 EC, with minor courses completing the balance. Study abroad can carry 30 EC, or 24 EC alongside a 6 EC Tilburg course.

components.name: Wicked Problems 301: Intervention Theories and Tools
Bachelor’s Thesis: Wicked Problems 303
components.note: The standard spring thesis requires at least 120 EC within the programme. Students conduct individual research with support from a thesis group and defend their work.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three options address organisational responses to social problems, international policy and displacement, or sustainability and social entrepreneurship. Their different organising questions are sustained by distinct course selections.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop financial accounting and management skills. Tilburg also teaches project management.
Both introduce social-science research design, measurement and empirical analysis.
Both connect survey design, measurement and quantitative analysis. UCR applies these methods to leadership and social experience.
Both examine motivation, teams, leadership and culture within organisations.
Both introduce sociological theories and apply them to social questions.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation.
Both study social influence, group behaviour and psychological research.
Both develop statistical analysis for social or behavioural data.
Both introduce economic reasoning about markets, choices and public intervention.
Both use regression to investigate empirical relationships. UCR also teaches instrumental variables in economic applications.
Both study public international law and institutions. Tilburg also incorporates EU law.
Both examine organisational change. UCR focuses on digital strategy and transformation.

notes.text: Tilburg combines organisation studies, human resource management, international law and research through a sequence on wicked problems and a required individual thesis. UCR offers related courses across these fields, with different emphases in each option.

audience.programmeDescription: Global Management of Social Issues at Tilburg University studies how organisations respond to complex problems such as inequality, migration and climate change. Students combine organisation studies, human resource management, law and social research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study through organisational responses to social problems, international policy and displacement, or sustainability and social entrepreneurship. Tilburg integrates these fields through its wicked-problems sequence, cross-cultural management and required thesis.
